title: Link, target, focus, hover, active states
learningObjectives: Explain link, target, focus, hover, active states and use selectors or sizing rules appropriately.

understand.concept: Link and interaction pseudo-classes include :link, :visited, :target, :hover, :focus, :focus-visible, and :active. They style elements based on navigation history, URL fragment targeting, or user interaction state. Their order and specificity can affect which rule wins.
understand.whyItMatters: Interaction states must remain perceivable for keyboard, pointer, and touch users. Do not rely only on hover, and maintain visible focus styling. Visited-link styling is restricted by browsers for privacy.
understand.analogy: These pseudo-classes are like signals that tell a control whether it is new, visited, selected by the URL, focused, or being pressed.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; selector matching and sizing follow CSS specifications and browser layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The links have distinct visited, hover, focus, and active states. The section matching the URL fragment receives :target styling.

examples.explanation: The links have distinct visited, hover, focus, and active states. The section matching the URL fragment receives :target styling.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example showing the selector or sizing behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Style a navigation link for hover and focus-visible. Add a :target style and test keyboard navigation without a mouse.
practise.independentTask: Build a short example that demonstrates the topic with realistic content. Inspect matched selectors or computed sizes in developer tools.
hints: Check which elements match each selector.
Avoid relying on decorative generated content for meaning.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-class matches the element identified by the URL fragment?
questions.explanation: :target matches the element whose ID corresponds to the current URL fragment.
